results.note: ingest-medium.yml mirrors ingest.yml's structure exactly: same triggers (schedule/workflow_dispatch/push paths), permissions, timeout-minutes:10, checkout/setup-python/setup-uv steps, and `uv run python -m ingest.heartbeat --tier <tier>` invocation pattern — only the cron string, job name, and heartbeat secret differ. Diffing the two files line-by-line confirms the practice is followed, not reinvented.

The diff touches zero lines of ingest/pipeline.py or ingest/registry.py. The medium tier is filtered by the pre-existing US-1201 predicate `definition.expected_update_interval_seconds == TIER_INTERVAL_SECONDS[tier]` (pipeline.py:364), reused unchanged via `--tier medium` (heartbeat.py:87 already accepted 'medium' as a choice before this story).

Research doc cites the vendor's own documented practice: 'Healthchecks.io "one check per job" with per-check Grace Time is the vendor's own documented best practice... https://healthchecks.io/docs/configuring_checks/' (10-research.md:20). Implementation matches it with a dedicated secret `HEALTHCHECK_URL_INGEST_MEDIUM` (ingest-medium.yml:27), distinct from the daily tier's `HEALTHCHECKS_PING_URL` and the canary's `HEALTHCHECK_URL_CONTRACT_CANARY`, asserted by the new test.

No test drives the assembled system through the real entry point for the medium tier. The genuine end-to-end pattern (mocking only I/O boundaries — psycopg.connect, httpx.get, and the vendor fetchers — then calling heartbeat.main(['--tier', X])) exists for daily (test_daily_tier_entry_point_persists_only_daily_board_rows_and_pings_once, line 1352) and for fast/SOL, but no equivalent 'medium' version was added. The only new test file, tests/test_ingest_medium_workflow.py, is a pure text-grep over the YAML file and never calls heartbeat.main or exercises run_ingestion/run_pipeline/run_scheduled_board. test_main_accepts_tier_argument (test_heartbeat.py:201) also doesn't count — it monkeypatches run_ingestion away entirely, so nothing downstream is actually wired or exercised.

No evidence of an actual GitHub Actions scheduled or dispatched run of ingest-medium.yml exists anywhere in the repo (events.ndjson, SESSION.md). This is the same structural gap flagged for US-1202-C5 before a human manually ran `gh workflow run` and cited the resulting run URL/conclusion — that same remediation has not happened for US-1203. Only a static YAML-text assertion (test_ingest_medium_workflow.py) exists, which does not satisfy a 'ci' method criterion requiring the real scheduled job.
Gate result 'US-1203-C6: exit 0 [uv run pytest -q]' confirms the full offline suite passes on current HEAD.

note: Two criteria fail: C4 has no true end-to-end test for the medium tier (only a YAML text-grep test was added; the same-pattern integration test that exists for daily/fast was never written for medium), and C5 has no evidence of a real completed/dispatched GitHub Actions run of ingest-medium.yml — this is the identical gap the human had to manually close for US-1202-C5, and it has not been closed here.
